content.title: Mission briefing
content.prompt:
You are given a blank HTML document.

Your job is to plan the structure for a small Forge course page.

The page must contain:

- a document title: `Forge Academy`
- a page heading: `Frontend Engineering`
- a short introductory paragraph
- a navigation region with links to `Curriculum` and `Practice`
- a main content area
- a section called `What you will learn`
- an unordered list with `HTML structure`, `page presentation`, and `page behavior`
- a section called `Start here`
- an ordered list with three steps
- a contact form with `Name` and `Email` fields
- a submit button labeled `Join the academy`
- a footer containing `Forge Academy`

Outline which semantic HTML elements you will choose for the document skeleton, page regions, lists, and form controls.
content.context: Lesson Focus: Forge Mission: Build the Page Structure — Independently construct a meaningful HTML document using the structures learned throughout the module.

content.question:
Predict the outer shape of the document.

Which structure makes the most sense?

options.text:
html
├── head
└── body
    ├── header
    ├── nav
    ├── main
    └── footer

codeSnippet.code:
html
├── head
└── body
    ├── header
    ├── nav
    ├── main
    └── footer

feedback.correct: Start with the document skeleton, then organize the visible page into meaningful regions.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. `<html>` is always the root element containing `<head>` followed by `<body>`, and visible page landmarks (`<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<footer>`) live inside `<body>`.

content.title: Build the skeleton
content.text:
Start with:

```html
<!doctype html>
<html>
  <head>
    <title>Forge Academy</title>
  </head>
  <body>
  </body>
</html>
```

Do not add anything else until this outer structure is correct.

activities.instruction: Complete the code challenge in the workspace, then run checks.

content.prompt:
Create the four top-level semantic page region landmarks in order:

```html
<header></header>
<nav></nav>
<main></main>
<footer></footer>
```

feedback.incorrect: Make sure all four landmark elements (`<header></header>`, `<nav></nav>`, `<main></main>`, and `<footer></footer>`) are present with opening and closing tags.

content.title: Final verification
content.text:
Use this checklist:

**Structure**

- [ ] The document starts with `<!doctype html>`.
- [ ] `<html>` contains `<head>` and `<body>`.
- [ ] The title is inside `<head>`.
- [ ] Page content is inside `<body>`.

**Meaning**

- [ ] The page has one main `<h1>`.
- [ ] Navigation links are inside `<nav>`.
- [ ] Primary page content is inside `<main>`.
- [ ] Related content is grouped in `<section>` elements.
- [ ] The footer uses `<footer>`.

**Lists**

- [ ] Topics use `<ul>`.
- [ ] Steps use `<ol>`.
- [ ] Every list item uses `<li>`.

**Form**

- [ ] The name label connects to `id="name"`.
- [ ] The email label connects to `id="email"`.
- [ ] The submit button uses `type="submit"`.

content.question:
Your page loads, but the “Start here” items appear as one block of text instead of three ordered steps.

What should you inspect first?

options.text: Whether the steps were placed inside an `<ol>` with `<li>` elements.
Whether the footer has the right text.
Whether the document title is correct.

feedback.correct: The symptom concerns list structure, so inspect the HTML elements that express that relationship.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. When list items collapse into a single paragraph-like block of text, the markup for the list (`<ol>` and `<li>` tags) is missing or malformed.

content.title: Transfer challenge
content.text:
A different product asks you to structure a “Recipe” page.

It needs:

- a page heading
- an ingredients list where order does not matter
- a numbered sequence of cooking steps
- a navigation area
- a main recipe area
- a footer

Without copying the Forge mission, name the element you would choose for each major piece.

**Strong answer:** `<h1>` for the main heading, `<ul>` and `<li>` for ingredients, `<ol>` and `<li>` for ordered cooking steps, `<nav>` for navigation, `<main>` for primary content, and `<footer>` for closing information.

content.title: Module mastery gate
content.text:
You have demonstrated the core HTML capability when you can build a small document without being told which element to use for every line.

You should be able to:

1. build the document skeleton,
2. choose elements by meaning,
3. nest content correctly,
4. use attributes for links, images, and form relationships,
5. organize content into meaningful page regions.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **HTML is not a pile of tags. It is a model of the document.**
The strongest HTML tells the truth about the content: what is a heading, what is navigation, what is the main content, what is a list, what is an input, and how those pieces relate.
**Senior habit:** Before adding another element, ask: “What is this content, and what relationship does it have to the surrounding content?”
nextSteps: Complete the lesson activities and demonstrate the target skill without relying on unseen concepts from later modules.

requirements: Screen-reader accessible code blocks and options
